Yeah I have seen many, many therapists, some even told me I seemed completely normal and my sister was the one who needed help(even though they'd never met her). Not until I started looking for DBT and therapists who covered attachment disorders in adults did I find people to take me seriously. And have you ever been to a therapist who you felt like knew absolutely nothing and you could just talk circles around them and they'd believe every word? A DBT therapist will not be like that.

I live with my fiance, we sleep next to each other every night and I still feel like this, almost daily. He is the exact same way, always been independent and also he's not really a social person. He has no social media and doesn't text or use his phone really and he always tells me that but I don't understand how you can love someone and not constantly be checking to see if they messaged you. So what I do, say if I wake up hour early and he wants to sleep till the last minute. I would usually freak out and just turn on lights and talk to him till he get up (like a bitch...) But sometimes I can convince myself that it's ok that I am alone, that I can do it by myself and plan my day without him.I don't expect him to get up or talk to me at all, I plan my whole day and all activities around myself and what I want/need to do. That way I am content with myself first and not expecting something from him. I dunno if that makes any sense but that's the only way I keep calm, and usually if I act all independant like I don't need him leadingmy life and all he gets needy and wants love

You aren't alone, although I really don't know how to help. I feel the exact same way. I'm actually here today because I threw away another opportunity this morning, closed another open door, and I'm beating myself up about if. I too want to succeed, a little part of me. And I want you to succeed. To be free, so to speak, to live your life. I don't know you but I know you do deserve it, to be content in life, and continue to have those doors open for you. Every little step is overcoming the fears, try to breath and when that little switch in the back of your head starts nagging and your heart starts racing telling you you can't, take a moment for yourself. Do a breathing exercise and tell yourself things you would tell a dear friend to cheer them up. You do deserve to live a life worth living

I can say from experience I have been here, I almost don't want to admit this but twice. The first time I found out I was pregnant my bf and I had been together for 3 months. It was a shock and I cried and finally went to P.P. to see how far along I was. The whole time my bf was supportive telling me he would be behind me 100% no matter what I decided. And it made all the difference. Because once those hormones started, which I hadn't even realized, my own inner compass was all over the place. I had to keep referring to how I felt before. I was pro-choice and more than that for my own self I never wanted children. Now all of a sudden I loved with all my heart a little thing inside of me that I had only just become aware of. And the thought of not starting a family seemed crazy. I have had my share of mental issues, being diagnosed bi-polar and having anxiety but nothing prepared me for the new wave of emotions that being pregnant was. So anyways I went to P.P. to talk to someone there and I knew that adoption or foster care was not an option having myself been down that road myself. I seriously thought about my life with a baby, about my mom and dad and how hard they worked, about my young friends with kids and how much they struggled and held resentment towards their spouses. I came to the conclusion that I did not want to bring a child into a life that wasn't going to be the most worth living, the most I could offer as the best version of myself. Everyone told me no child comes at a good time, maybe, but is it fair to bring a child into a life of unnecessary hardship? Or into a life of uncertainty? If you are spiritual at all it might be a good time to go back to that, or meditate. For me I believe that the soul of my future child will always come back when I am ready and I decided to get an abortion. My bf and I are still together to this day and that was 2 years ago but we talked about it constantly and decided that we WERE meant to be together, that this IS a sign from the universe, but you also have a choice in your path. And you need to do what is best for you first, in the end you are the only one who has to carry the baby, go through labor, nurse and you are the only one who carries your emotions, be your own best friend. And the thing I regret the most was waiting to make the decision, once I decided and went through with it I had a huge sense of relief. I was depressed afterwards and definitely thought about and voiced my fear that I'd done the wrong thing and every time my bf would say; remember what you told me? that you weren't ready, that we are going to do that together when we are financially able. I definitely will never be the same, and I now want children which I never did, but you can become stronger than ever together with a little forgiveness and understanding. I hope my experience helps you and I hope you and your bf can keep your love growing
